pages.title: The Pot Is a Black Box
pages.text: A ceramic melting pot melts open to the fire with nothing to hold its dirt back, so it keeps its melt down to **10% slag** no matter how clean the charge was: nothing poured out of a pot is ever pure metal, and it costs you a tenth of the charge as fire loss.$p$pIt is still forgiving: the ratio bands are wide, so a pot pour becomes Flawed metal rather than junk.

pages.title: Pouring Out of a Pot
pages.text: Right-click the pot while its contents are molten to open it, and put a mold into the slots there. While the bath holds liquid the pot is not an inventory any more, so the same gesture does not show you the four item slots.$p$pMelted parts and ingots keep their dirt when you re-melt them, so a pot's output stays dirty through the loop. Melting an object is a way to move metal, never a way to clean it.

pages.title: The Crucible Is the Alloyer
pages.text: The crucible is where proportions are decided: it holds what its melt was made of, it dilutes a flawed batch with better metal, and it pours measured amounts into a mold. What it cannot do is take dirt out - it pours from the top, so whatever floats in the bath goes into the pour with the metal.$p$pPicked up, a crucible keeps what its melt was made of, so a flawed pour in a chest does not forget its own composition.
